ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: Room temperature so they cook evenly

steps.instruction: Soften the diced onion and sliced pepper in olive oil over medium heat until the edges brown.
Push vegetables aside, bloom cumin and paprika with the garlic in the oil for 30 seconds until fragrant.
steps.tips: This is the flavor step most recipes skip — don't let the garlic burn.

steps.instruction: Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer until the sauce thickens enough to hold a trench.
Make four wells, crack an egg into each, cover, and cook until whites set but yolks stay loose.
steps.tips: Cover with a lid or foil — steam sets the whites from above.

steps.instruction: Finish with parsley and a drizzle of oil; serve straight from the pan with bread.

tips.text: The sauce is ready for eggs when a spoon dragged through it leaves a trench that holds for two seconds.
Feta crumbled in at step 4 turns this into the richer Israeli café version.
Sauce (without eggs) keeps 4 days refrigerated — re-simmer and add fresh eggs to serve.

substitutions.substitute: Whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand

synthesis_response.tldr: One-pan shakshuka in 25 minutes, built on a spice-blooming step and a trench-test sauce.
keyTakeaways: Bloom the spices in oil before the tomatoes for deeper flavor
The sauce is ready when a spoon-trench holds for two seconds
Cover the pan so steam sets the whites while yolks stay runny
